title: Mitchell TTX · HVAA protection
subtitle: Pulse support · Ambush alert · Decoy operations
description: Illustrates the three published HVAA-protect team lines of effort from the 2024 Mitchell TTX (Figures 6–8, report pp. 19–20). The team sought to protect E-7A Wedgetail and air refueling aircraft against PLA long-range air-threat networks, using CCA together with F-22s and F-15EX.
assumptions: Published LOE 1: F-22s and air-to-air/EW CCA in support of strike pulses; F-15EX air-launched CCA from Guam and recoverable EW CCA re-use from the Ryukyus (Figure 6).
Published LOE 2: reactive expendable CCA waves with recoverable ISR/EW CCA between pulses; Figure 7 discusses up to four waves a day depending on target availability.
Published LOE 3: recoverable ISR/EW CCA decoys and surveillance intended to keep PLA defenses uncertain (Figure 8).
Display timeline is not a validated exercise time trace; map positions, paths and actor counts remain illustrative. No target detection, interceptions or combat outcomes are modeled.

phases.title: LOE 1 · HVAA pulse support
phases.narrative: CCA and F-22s were proposed to counter KJ-500 and airborne threats to E-7A and tankers during strikes.

phases.title: LOE 2 · Ambush alert
phases.narrative: Reactive expendable air-to-air CCA supported by recoverable EW/ISR CCA would maintain pressure between strikes.

phases.title: LOE 3 · Decoy operations
phases.narrative: Recoverable EW and ISR CCA were intended to compel PLA defensive responses and identify targets of opportunity.

phases.title: LOEs recur intermittently
phases.narrative: Cycle reset visualizes concurrent and repeated concepts, not actual sortie timing.
